overview: Black allows a big e4-d4 centre and builds a Philidor- or Pirc-like set-up with ...e6 and ...d6, then ...Nf6, ...Be7 and ...O-O or a ...g6 fianchetto. White develops naturally with Nf3, Nc3 and Be2 or goes for a kingside attack. Black is cramped but tries to break with ...c5 or ...e5. It is a rare move-order, strong players seldom choose it.

white_ideas.idea: Take space with Nc3, Nf3, Be3 and Qd2, with kingside attack or e5

typical_structures.structure: White e4/d4 against Black d6/e6; Philidor, Pirc or Hanham-like set-ups

character.notes: Passive and cramped; Black is hard to crack quickly but I expect no forcing play.

structure.notes: Centre tension persists until ...c5 or ...e5: flexible.

approach.notes: Strong players seldom use it; a move-order surprise.

level.notes: Nothing to memorise but passive; intermediate by default.

character.reason: Compact, passive pawn structure, hard to break but cramped.

level.reason: Few lines to learn but passive plans.

plans.reason: White's extra space in the centre is the main theme.
